title: Symbolic regression of the best confirmed controllers' latents
description: The concepts of compact's discovery controllers, recovered by symbolic regression (experiments/ground.py concepts, PySR 2.7.2) from the grounding of the confirmed controllers (release exp-ground-rl-confirm-32, their own rollouts, no new rollouts). By the owner's direction the concepts come from the best-trained networks (docs/methodology.md, grounding). The three best per teacher by the score each run left in the confirmation (exp-controller-rl-confirm-31, log utility minus the fixed rule on the validation links; every run is scored on the same episodes, so the order against BBRv3 is the same), chosen before this run: from Cubic, ctl-cubic-k7-s2 (-0.129), ctl-cubic-k16-s2 (-0.140) and ctl-cubic-k10-s1 (-0.147); from BBRv3, ctl-bbr3-k7-s2 (-0.161), ctl-bbr3-k7-s1 (-0.211) and ctl-bbr3-k7-s3 (-0.233). For each latent, PySR searches for a formula over the window in force, in packets, and the 8 features of the three networks' pooled path without the sender's measurements, in ms, Mbit/s or kB, with +, -, *, / and log, at most 20 nodes, 60 iterations, on 4000 rows of the training links' rollouts; the formula kept is the simplest on PySR's front within 0.01 of the best R^2 on the validation links, and it reads the path when it uses more than the window. The window is an input rather than taken out first: an earlier version of this file took it out by a linear fit, which left most of its effect in what PySR fitted, and recovered no latent. Rules fixed before the run: a formula is well recovered at an R^2 of 0.8 or more on the validation links; the single best network's concepts are its well-recovered formulas; the pooled concepts are the well-recovered formulas of all three, where of formulas whose values correlate above 0.9 in absolute value the simplest is kept. PySR's search is multithreaded and so not bit-reproducible; the seed is fixed per latent. Whether these networks are trained well against BBRv3 is measured by experiments/versus-bbr3.json; this run is a first read of the method. The runner's own Julia cannot load its system image, so a stub julia that fails stands first on PATH and PySR installs the Julia it pins. The test links are not read.
run: case "$TEACHER" in cubic) R="ctl-cubic-k7-s2 ctl-cubic-k16-s2 ctl-cubic-k10-s1";; bbr3) R="ctl-bbr3-k7-s2 ctl-bbr3-k7-s1 ctl-bbr3-k7-s3";; *) exit 2;; esac; NJ="$(mktemp -d)"; printf "#!/bin/sh\nexit 1\n" > "$NJ/julia"; chmod +x "$NJ/julia"; PATH="$NJ:$PATH" uv run --with pysr==2.7.2 python experiments/ground.py concepts "$OUT/concepts-$TEACHER" --runs $(for r in $R; do printf "%s " "$IN/runs/$r"; done)
